subject: Follow-up: traffic profile + GPU selection for Dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Casey Taylor <ctaylor@finora.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: traffic profile + GPU selection for Dedicated capacity

Hi Casey —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we can size Dedicated correctly and avoid surprises during the PoC. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary of what I heard:
- Target feature: real-time personalized insights delivered in-app (both interactive chat and async batch jobs).
- Typical prompt/response token mix: average prompt ~80 tokens, average response ~450 tokens; about 18–25% of requests return long outputs (>2k tokens) for in-depth reports.
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~75 TPS (inference requests per second), 5–10% sustained concurrency spikes to ~220 TPS, and occasional daily peaks up to ~320 TPS for scheduled batch re-runs.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 400ms for chat/short queries, longer tolerated for bulk report generation.
- Data controls: must run in a VPC for production; PII redaction handled upstream.

Questions we still need from you to firm up sizing:
1) Can you share the token mix CSV you mentioned (prompt/response histograms and peak window distribution)? a sample anonymized export is fine.
2) For the long-output requests, are those mostly single long responses (one call with 2k+ tokens), or pipelined multi-call sessions?
3) Expected concurrency per user session vs total concurrency (helps estimate KV cache pressure).

Preliminary sizing notes (for discussion with infra):
- Given the token mix and peak TPS, two H100s (with high-memory configs) would comfortably cover throughput and long-token workloads, but 3–4x A100 80GB nodes may be more cost-effective if you can tolerate slightly higher p95 during peak bursts.
- We should measure effective tokens/sec per GPU using a sampled prompt set — the PoC can run a short synthetic load to verify.

Next steps I propose:
- You send the anonymized token mix CSV (attachment name suggestion: finora_token_mix_v1.csv).
- We (Redwood) return a short PoC worksheet and a compare-run: H100 x2 vs A100 x4 cost/latency tradeoff.
- Schedule a 30-min sizing call later this week after you upload the CSV.

I attached the PoC template and a quick worksheet to fill; I can pre-populate with the numbers you send.

Best,
Karthik
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
(k) 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood_poc_template.pdf (PoC worksheet), finora_token_mix_v1.csv (placeholder to attach)

Subject: Re: Follow-up: traffic profile + GPU selection for Dedicated capacity

Thanks Karthik —

Appreciate the clear recap. Confirming the majority of long outputs are single-call long responses (users request a full narrative report in one completion). We do have some workflows that fan-out into multiple calls (analytics pipelines), but those are background batch jobs and can be scheduled.

I've uploaded a scrubbed CSV to our shared Drive with daily histograms and a 7-day rolling peak window. Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Finora-example

Short answers to your Qs:
1) CSV uploaded (see link).
2) Long outputs: single-call in ~85% of cases, rest are multi-call batch.
3) Concurrency: average per-session concurrency is low (1–2), total concurrent sessions drive overall TPS. Peak bursts correlate to a morning sync and a nightly batch job.

One more constraint: our procurement prefers not to commit to H100 if A100 can meet the SLOs at reasonable cost. We asked infra to provide their preferred roofing (A100 favored).

Let us know when you can run the comparison. We can open an engineering channel with temporary access to a representative prompt set for the test.

-Casey

Marissa / Dylan —

See Casey's answers and the Drive link. Procurement leans A100; Finora prefers cost predictability. Can you run a quick back-of-envelope comparing:
- 2x H100 (assume model = open-Large-8b-quant) vs 4x A100 80GB (same model + quant)
- Inputs: avg prompt 80 tokens, avg response 450 tokens, long outputs 2k tokens at 20% frequency, steady 75 TPS, peak 320 TPS (5–10 minute duration)
- Provide expected p95 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, and ballpark monthly cost (infra only) for each configuration.

If we can show similar p95 with A100 at >20% cost savings, that's our angle.

Thanks — KR
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Casey Taylor <ctaylor@finora.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@finora.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: traffic profile + GPU selection for Dedicated capacity

Thanks for the context, all —

We ran a quick estimate using the sample set Casey uploaded and our internal perf kernels for the model family you mentioned. High-level findings (quick summary, will follow with a populated PoC worksheet):

Configuration A — 2x H100 (prod-grade memory):
- Expected steady-state throughput headroom: ~240 TPS (comfortably covers avg + spike buffer).
- p95 latency for average queries: ~260–320ms; long outputs p95 ~1.1–1.6s depending on tokenization variance.
- Best for operators wanting headroom and simpler long-token handling.
- Infra cost estimate (monthly, GPU-only): ~$48k.

Configuration B — 4x A100 80GB (cost-optimized):
- Expected steady-state throughput headroom: ~300 TPS (higher aggregate due to more cards) but less per-card long-token headroom.
- p95 latency for average queries: ~320–420ms; long outputs p95 ~1.6–2.4s and may show increased variance under peak bursts.
- More cost-effective for bursty workloads if you accept slightly higher p95 on long outputs.
- Infra cost estimate (monthly, GPU-only): ~$33k.

Recommendation: Run the short PoC comparing both configurations under a 30-minute mixed workload (replicate 20% long outputs and a 10-minute peak window at 320 TPS). We'll populate the PoC worksheet and propose a 48-hour window for the trial.

Attaching the populated worksheet (redwood_poc_template_filled.pdf) and a short run plan. Could you confirm procurement constraints (contract length, pre-pay vs monthly) so we include that in the final estimate?

Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through the numbers.

—Marissa
